questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.topic: Diuretics & drugs acting on the kidney
questions.stem: Furosemide acts on which part of the nephron?
options: The thick ascending limb of the loop of Henle, inhibiting the Na-K-2Cl cotransporter
questions.concept: Loop diuretics are the most efficacious, blocking reabsorption of up to 25% of filtered sodium and abolishing the medullary concentration gradient, hence their use in pulmonary oedema and volume overload.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.topic: Diuretics & drugs acting on the kidney
questions.stem: Thiazide diuretics characteristically cause:
options: Hypokalaemia, hyponatraemia, hyperuricaemia, hyperglycaemia and hyperlipidaemia
questions.concept: Thiazides reduce urinary calcium, making them useful in recurrent calcium stones and osteoporosis, but raise urate, glucose and lipids. Loop diuretics conversely increase calcium excretion.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.topic: Diuretics & drugs acting on the kidney
questions.stem: Spironolactone is a:
options: Competitive aldosterone antagonist causing potassium retention and gynaecomastia
questions.concept: Spironolactone is used in heart failure, ascites of cirrhosis, primary hyperaldosteronism and resistant hypertension. Gynaecomastia and menstrual irregularity result from antiandrogenic action; eplerenone is more selective.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.topic: Diuretics & drugs acting on the kidney
questions.stem: Mannitol is contraindicated in:
options: Acute pulmonary oedema and established anuria
questions.concept: An osmotic diuretic expands intravascular volume before diuresis, precipitating pulmonary oedema in cardiac failure. It is filtered but not reabsorbed, and is ineffective if the kidneys are not producing urine.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.topic: Diuretics & drugs acting on the kidney
questions.stem: Acetazolamide produces diuresis by:
options: Inhibiting carbonic anhydrase, causing bicarbonate loss and metabolic acidosis
questions.concept: Its diuretic effect is weak and self-limiting as acidosis develops, so it is mainly used in glaucoma, acute mountain sickness and to alkalinise urine in salicylate poisoning.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.topic: Diuretics & drugs acting on the kidney
questions.stem: Ototoxicity is a particular risk with which diuretic, especially with aminoglycosides?
questions.concept: Loop diuretics alter endolymph electrolyte composition causing dose-related, usually reversible deafness, markedly potentiated by concurrent aminoglycosides which are also ototoxic and nephrotoxic.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.topic: Diuretics & drugs acting on the kidney
questions.stem: In a patient on digoxin, the danger of thiazide or loop diuretics is:
questions.concept: Potassium competes with digoxin for binding to the Na-K-ATPase, so hypokalaemia enhances binding and toxicity. Potassium supplementation or a potassium-sparing diuretic is added.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.topic: Diuretics & drugs acting on the kidney
questions.stem: Desmopressin is used in diabetes insipidus because it:
options: Is a selective V2 receptor agonist with antidiuretic action and minimal vasopressor effect
questions.concept: Selectivity for renal V2 receptors avoids the vasoconstriction of vasopressin. It is also used in mild haemophilia A and von Willebrand disease, where it releases factor VIII and vWF from endothelium.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.topic: Diuretics & drugs acting on the kidney
questions.stem: Tolvaptan is used in hyponatraemia because it:
options: Blocks V2 receptors causing free water excretion without sodium loss
questions.concept: Vaptans produce aquaresis, raising serum sodium in SIADH and hypervolaemic hyponatraemia. Correction must be gradual to avoid osmotic demyelination, and liver toxicity limits long-term use.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.topic: Diuretics & drugs acting on the kidney
questions.stem: Amiloride and triamterene are potassium-sparing because they:
options: Block epithelial sodium channels in the collecting duct, independent of aldosterone
questions.concept: Unlike spironolactone they act directly on the ENaC channel, so they work even when aldosterone is absent. All potassium-sparing agents risk hyperkalaemia, especially with ACE inhibitors or renal impairment.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.topic: GIT drugs: antiemetics, antacids/PPIs, laxatives, antidiarrhoeals
questions.stem: Proton pump inhibitors act by:
options: Irreversibly inhibiting the H+/K+ ATPase of the gastric parietal cell
questions.concept: PPIs are prodrugs activated in the acidic canaliculus, so they are most effective taken 30 to 60 minutes before a meal when proton pumps are actively secreting. Acid suppression lasts beyond the plasma half-life.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.topic: GIT drugs: antiemetics, antacids/PPIs, laxatives, antidiarrhoeals
questions.stem: Long-term proton pump inhibitor therapy is associated with:
options: Hypomagnesaemia, B12 deficiency, fracture risk and Clostridioides difficile infection
questions.concept: Reduced acidity impairs absorption of magnesium, B12, calcium and iron and removes a barrier to enteric infection, so PPIs should be reviewed periodically and used at the lowest effective dose.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.topic: GIT drugs: antiemetics, antacids/PPIs, laxatives, antidiarrhoeals
questions.stem: Ondansetron acts as an antiemetic by:
options: Blocking 5-HT3 receptors in the chemoreceptor trigger zone and gut
questions.concept: It is highly effective for chemotherapy and postoperative vomiting with no extrapyramidal effects, but causes headache, constipation and QT prolongation. It is ineffective for motion sickness.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.topic: GIT drugs: antiemetics, antacids/PPIs, laxatives, antidiarrhoeals
questions.stem: Metoclopramide should be used cautiously in young patients because it causes:
options: Acute dystonic reactions from central D2 blockade
questions.concept: Oculogyric crisis and torticollis occur particularly in children and young women, treated with promethazine or an anticholinergic. Domperidone does not cross the blood-brain barrier well and causes fewer such effects, but prolongs QT.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.topic: GIT drugs: antiemetics, antacids/PPIs, laxatives, antidiarrhoeals
questions.stem: The drug of choice for motion sickness is:
options: Hyoscine (scopolamine) or an antihistamine such as promethazine
questions.concept: Motion sickness is mediated by vestibular cholinergic and histaminergic pathways, so anticholinergics and antihistamines work, whereas 5-HT3 blockers and prokinetics do not. Prophylactic dosing before travel is essential.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.topic: GIT drugs: antiemetics, antacids/PPIs, laxatives, antidiarrhoeals
questions.stem: Aluminium and magnesium antacids are usually combined because:
options: Aluminium causes constipation and magnesium causes diarrhoea, so effects offset
questions.concept: The combination gives predictable bowel habit. Aluminium accumulates in renal failure causing encephalopathy and osteomalacia, and antacids reduce absorption of tetracyclines, fluoroquinolones and iron.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.topic: GIT drugs: antiemetics, antacids/PPIs, laxatives, antidiarrhoeals
questions.stem: Loperamide is preferred over diphenoxylate as an antidiarrhoeal because it:
options: Does not cross the blood-brain barrier significantly, so has minimal central opioid effects
questions.concept: Loperamide acts on gut mu receptors slowing transit. Both are contraindicated in dysentery, suspected Clostridioides difficile colitis and in children, where they can cause toxic megacolon and respiratory depression.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.topic: GIT drugs: antiemetics, antacids/PPIs, laxatives, antidiarrhoeals
questions.stem: Lactulose is used in hepatic encephalopathy because it:
options: Acidifies colonic contents trapping ammonia as ammonium and acts as an osmotic laxative
questions.concept: Colonic bacteria ferment lactulose to lactic and acetic acid, converting NH3 to poorly absorbed NH4+ while purging it. Rifaximin, a poorly absorbed antibiotic, reduces ammonia-producing flora.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.topic: GIT drugs: antiemetics, antacids/PPIs, laxatives, antidiarrhoeals
questions.stem: Sucralfate is most effective when given:
options: On an empty stomach, as it requires an acidic environment to polymerise
questions.concept: Sucralfate polymerises in acid to form a viscous protective barrier over the ulcer base, so concurrent antacids or PPIs reduce its efficacy and it should be given at least two hours apart from other drugs.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.topic: GIT drugs: antiemetics, antacids/PPIs, laxatives, antidiarrhoeals
questions.stem: Bulk-forming laxatives such as ispaghula require:
options: Adequate fluid intake, as inadequate fluid risks intestinal obstruction
questions.concept: They act by increasing stool bulk and are the safest for long-term use, but must be avoided in suspected obstruction or faecal impaction, and are taken with plenty of water.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.topic: Asthma & COPD drugs, antitussives & antihistamines
questions.stem: The drug of choice for an acute asthma attack is:
options: Inhaled short-acting beta-2 agonist such as salbutamol
questions.concept: Salbutamol relaxes bronchial smooth muscle within minutes via beta-2 receptors. Inhaled steroids are controllers, not relievers, and cromoglycate is prophylactic only, useless in an acute attack.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.topic: Asthma & COPD drugs, antitussives & antihistamines
questions.stem: Inhaled corticosteroids are the cornerstone of asthma control because they:
options: Suppress airway inflammation, reducing exacerbations and airway remodelling
questions.concept: Local delivery gives high airway concentrations with limited systemic effects; mouth rinsing after use prevents oral candidiasis and dysphonia. High doses can still suppress growth and the adrenal axis.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.topic: Asthma & COPD drugs, antitussives & antihistamines
questions.stem: Long-acting beta-2 agonists must never be used alone in asthma because:
options: Monotherapy is associated with increased asthma-related death
questions.concept: LABAs relieve symptoms while inflammation progresses unchecked, masking deterioration. They are always combined with an inhaled corticosteroid in a single inhaler to ensure this cannot happen.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.topic: Asthma & COPD drugs, antitussives & antihistamines
questions.stem: Theophylline has a narrow therapeutic index, with toxicity manifesting as:
questions.concept: Levels are raised by erythromycin, ciprofloxacin, cimetidine and heart failure, and lowered by smoking and rifampicin. Its narrow index and interactions have reduced its role to a third-line agent.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.topic: Asthma & COPD drugs, antitussives & antihistamines
questions.stem: Ipratropium bromide is particularly useful in:
options: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, where vagal tone is the main reversible component
questions.concept: Antimuscarinics block the dominant reversible cholinergic bronchoconstriction of COPD. Long-acting agents such as tiotropium reduce exacerbations, and their systemic absorption is minimal.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.topic: Asthma & COPD drugs, antitussives & antihistamines
questions.stem: Montelukast acts by:
questions.concept: Leukotriene receptor antagonists are especially useful in aspirin-sensitive asthma and exercise-induced bronchoconstriction, are given orally, and are a useful add-on in children. Neuropsychiatric effects are a recognised concern.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.topic: Asthma & COPD drugs, antitussives & antihistamines
questions.stem: Second-generation antihistamines such as cetirizine and loratadine are preferred because they:
options: Cause less sedation as they poorly cross the blood-brain barrier
questions.concept: First-generation agents like chlorpheniramine and promethazine are sedating and anticholinergic, which is a disadvantage in daytime use but exploited for motion sickness, vertigo and as hypnotics.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.topic: Asthma & COPD drugs, antitussives & antihistamines
questions.stem: Omalizumab is used in severe allergic asthma because it:
options: Is a monoclonal antibody that binds free IgE
questions.concept: By binding free IgE it prevents mast cell sensitisation, reducing exacerbations in severe allergic asthma with raised IgE. Mepolizumab targets IL-5 in eosinophilic asthma, a different biological phenotype.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.topic: Asthma & COPD drugs, antitussives & antihistamines
questions.stem: Codeine as an antitussive acts by:
questions.concept: Codeine and dextromethorphan are central antitussives; codeine causes constipation and dependence and is contraindicated in children under 12 and in nursing mothers who are ultra-rapid CYP2D6 metabolisers.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.topic: Asthma & COPD drugs, antitussives & antihistamines
questions.stem: Beta blockers are contraindicated in asthma because:
options: Blockade of bronchial beta-2 receptors causes bronchospasm
questions.concept: Even cardioselective beta-1 blockers lose selectivity at higher doses, and topical timolol eye drops have precipitated fatal asthma, so any beta blocker must be used with great caution.
